slot.brief: Ice/water mixture with heat loss/gain plus phase change; find final temperature or fraction melted

stem: Water of mass $M$ at $T^\circ\text{C}$ is added to $m$ ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$ in an insulated calorimeter of heat capacity $C$, initially at $0^\circ\text{C}$. If all the ice melts and the final temperature is above zero, find it. The specific heat of water is $s$ and the latent heat of fusion is $L$.

verdicts.working: Energy balance: $Ms(T-t)=mL+mst+Ct$. Hence $t=\dfrac{MsT-mL}{(M+m)s+C}$, which is option A.

working:
$Ms(T-T_f)=mL+(ms+C)T_f$; hence $T_f=\dfrac{MsT-mL}{(M+m)s+C}$.

Independent check: Energy balance: $Ms(T-t)=mL+mst+Ct$. Hence $t=\dfrac{MsT-mL}{(M+m)s+C}$, which is option A.
solution:
By conservation of heat, heat lost by water equals heat used to melt the ice and warm the melted ice and calorimeter:
$$Ms(T-T_f)=mL+(ms+C)T_f$$
Rearranging gives $T_f=\dfrac{MsT-mL}{(M+m)s+C}$.
